name: ISO/IEC 42001:2023
_note_future_trigger: This overlay will also be available as a certification_target in a future release. Currently wired as data_classification triggered by DC-AI.
description: ISO/IEC 42001 AI Management System Standard overlay. The ISO 27001 equivalent for AI. Provides requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an AI management system (AIMS). Activated by AI training data declarations.

evidence_requirements: AI policy established, approved by top management, and communicated (Clause 5.2)
AI management system scope defined and documented (Clause 4.3)
Management commitment to responsible AI development evidenced (Clause 5.1)
Roles, responsibilities, and authorities for AIMS assigned and communicated (Clause 5.3)
Competence requirements for AI-related roles defined and evaluated (Clause 7.2)
Accountability structure documented in organizational chart or responsibility matrix
AI risk assessment process established addressing AI-specific risks (Clause 6.1)
Risk criteria and acceptance thresholds defined by management (Clause 6.1.1)
Risk treatment plan documented with selected controls and justification (Clause 6.1.3)
Human oversight mechanisms defined for AI system operation (Clause 8.4)
Decision points requiring human review identified and documented
Management review of AIMS conducted at planned intervals (Clause 9.3)
Inventory of AI systems maintained with documented intended purposes (Annex A MAP 1.1)
AI system lifecycle stages documented — development, deployment, operation, retirement
AI system awareness ensured among relevant personnel (Clause 7.3)
Resources needed for AIMS determined and provided (Clause 7.1)
Third-party AI components and tools documented
Data documentation for AI systems — sources, quality, representativeness, known biases (Annex A MAP 1.5)
Data management procedures established for training, testing, and validation data
Data lifecycle documented from acquisition through disposal
Third-party AI component assessment conducted (Annex A MAP 5.1)
Supply chain risks specific to AI evaluated — model providers, data sources, tool dependencies
Due diligence on external AI components documented
AI-specific risk assessment including impact on individuals and society (Annex A MAP 1.1)
Risk assessment considers AI-specific threats — bias, drift, adversarial manipulation, hallucination
Impact assessment documented for high-risk AI applications
Access controls for AI systems and data proportionate to risk level
Authentication mechanisms documented in AIMS procedures
AI system operational boundaries documented and enforced (Clause 8.4)
Scope constraints aligned with intended purpose documentation
AI system development lifecycle documented with change management (Clause 8.1)
Version control and traceability for AI components maintained
Data protection measures documented in AI system design (Annex A MAP 1.5)
Privacy considerations integrated into AI system lifecycle
Monitoring and measurement of AIMS processes documented (Annex A MEA 2.1)
Records of AI system operation maintained as documented information (Clause 7.5)
Audit trail enables traceability of AI system decisions
Operational planning and control procedures documented (Clause 8.1)
Configuration management integrated into AI system lifecycle
Information security controls applied to AI systems per organizational policy
Encryption and access controls proportionate to data sensitivity
AI system robustness measures documented (Clause 8.4)
Input validation and error handling for AI system inputs documented
AI system performance monitored against defined metrics (Annex A MEA 2.2)
Anomaly detection for AI system behavior — accuracy degradation, bias emergence, drift
Monitoring results documented and analyzed at planned intervals
AI system configuration changes detected and evaluated (Clause 8.1)
Monitoring covers AI-specific configuration — model parameters, training data, feature sets
Internal audit of AIMS conducted at planned intervals (Clause 9.2)
Performance evaluation against AIMS objectives documented (Clause 9.1)
Management review includes assessment of AIMS suitability and effectiveness (Clause 9.3)
Documented information integrity controls in place (Clause 7.5.3)
AI system records protected against unauthorized modification
AI incident management procedure established (Annex A MAN 4.1)
Incident categorization and response procedures specific to AI failures documented
Response procedures cover AI-specific incidents — model failures, bias incidents, safety events
Escalation procedures for AI incidents documented (Annex A MAN 4.1)
Communication procedures for AI-related incidents defined
AI incident evidence preserved per AIMS documented information requirements (Clause 7.5)
Incident records maintained for analysis and improvement
Recovery procedures for AI system failures documented
Rollback capability to previous known-good AI system state
Nonconformities addressed with corrective actions (Clause 10.1)
Continual improvement of AIMS demonstrated through documented evidence (Clause 10.2)
Lessons learned from AI incidents integrated into risk assessment and control updates (Annex A MAN 4.2)

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: Certification audit by accredited certification body. Stage 1 (documentation review) and Stage 2 (implementation audit). Surveillance audits annually. Recertification every 3 years.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Accredited certification body. Audit results reported to management for management review (Clause 9.3).

human_oversight_mandates.description: ISO 42001 does not mandate specific human oversight configurations but requires management review (Clause 9.3), monitoring of AIMS effectiveness (Clause 9.1), and organizational awareness of AI system impacts (Clause 7.3). Human oversight is an outcome of the management system, not a prescriptive requirement.

notes: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is the AI management system standard — the ISO 27001 equivalent for AI. It is process-oriented, emphasizing documented procedures, management review records, and continuous improvement evidence. Unlike PCI which is checklist-oriented, ISO 42001 wants to see the management system operating. Certification requires demonstrating the Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle. Published December 2023, with growing adoption among organizations pursuing responsible AI credentials.
